chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Musicians as the neighborhood heroes and the cutting contests
summary: Danny says every New Orleans kid wanted to be a musician, admiring Manuel Perez and Chris Kelly and watching Kid Rena and Kid Ricotti battle on the corner.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: other sports. But in New Orleans, when I come up, other than playing in the street, when you got down to something you want to do that you aspire... Like, today kids aspire to be, if they're tall...to be a basketball star. If he's heavy, he's going to be a football star. Well, I had no... none of that I was involved with. Everything I saw, everybody, they wanted to be a musician. Because you saw the musicians walking there. Everything was music. Music. Music. Music...
And they got the best of everything, too, didn't they?
Yeah. Well, everything was good... It was the glamour... The glamour stick(?) was not a Jackie Robinson or a Joe Louis or...or Abba-Dabba, that...

None of them people. This was who was... Mister Manuel Perez, when he'd blow that trumpet...cornet in the street, and everybody said, "That's Mister Manuel Perez blowing." Or you saw Chris Kelly on a truck, playing them Blues. You'd say, "I'd like to do that." You'd see how them people get affected by that music. You'd say, "Mister Chris really blows. Did you hear him play? Yeah, Mister

Chris, Lordy." See? And you heard that. And you'd see Kid Rena, and you'd see a battle of music -- Kid Rena and Kid Ricotti(?), cousins, but that don't make no difference, 'cause the blood's gonna fly if they meet today. And they're both advertised in the same neighborhood. And here come Chris Kelly. And here come Long-Haired Bob with his truck or on his wagon. And them cats meet on the corner, and they're battlin' to draw a crowd of about four or five hundred people. They stand there and they blow. And they were so into his blowing, but "He should go home because he's no...he can't compete with so-and-so." And you're hearing this all the time.
